name: Tomas Hansen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm a senior field researcher with the Work Futures Panel. We're independent of AI firms, employers, unions, political parties and government; we don't sell or campaign. Your answers are confidential, including the parts you wouldn't say at work. What is a normal day like for you?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead four waste-reporting clerks inside a large food manufacturer. The weighbridge sends numbers, and my team turns them into reports on spoiled food and collections, but the signed ticket can disagree with the screen. I moved from delivery coordination into this junior lead post recently, and accounting codes still catch me out. I have a bachelor's degree and use AI every day for drafts, then check the ticket myself.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What does home look like now?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 58 and live with my partner Mira, who works in a school kitchen. Our son and daughter are grown and live in separate homes; we have a mortgage. My manager pay is about typical, we have four months of expenses saved, and there are some similar firms nearby. Retirement is in sight but we have not checked either pension's date or amount.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A modest tool already sorts our weekly food-waste forms, and I still check the weighbridge tickets before the report goes upstairs. Our mortgage is paid from my manager wage and Mira's school-kitchen pay, and we have four months of expenses saved. If nothing radical changes, I expect to keep learning this lead job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the four reporting clerks that a weight estimate must trace to the original ticket. I'd tell the staff association representative our current AI summary still needs a person's signature. I wouldn't claim a tidy chart means less food was thrown away.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I use AI every day for first drafts, but I am new to managing the reporting team and still miss some accounting rules. The work looks steady in a plateau, and there are a few similar offices nearby if this plant changes. Four months cash and Mira's pay make the mortgage feel manageable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: On Monday I'll compare the eleven waste loads flagged as unusually light with their signed weighbridge tickets. I'll keep reviewing the existing AI summaries for the first plateau year and put 120 monthly into cash only after our mortgage, food and medicine are covered by paid wages. I'll show any corrected figures to the staff association representative before the next report.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about work and the bills. I still dislike a chart that makes a missing pallet look like progress.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What was wrong with a light load?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One ticket was for the empty truck, and the form called it a low-waste day. The night crew had actually thrown away spoiled flour after a cooler failed. An empty truck is not an environmental achievement.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How did you reach this role?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I spent years coordinating deliveries, then moved to this junior reporting lead job when the old desk closed. I have a bachelor's degree and can read a route sheet faster than an accounts code. Mira and I are 58; our children are grown and pay their own bills.

I'd show the **staff association** any corrected waste figures.
think: My new lead work looks **steady** in a plateau.
Four months cash and Mira's pay make **our mortgage** manageable.
do: Check **eleven light loads** against signed weighbridge tickets Monday.
Review the **existing AI summaries** before reports go upstairs.
Save **120 monthly** only after mortgage, food and medicine are paid from wages.
feel: I feel **calm** about work and household bills.
S0.quote: An empty truck is not an environmental achievement.
fieldNote: He catches a false low-waste claim using an **empty-truck ticket**.
He uses AI **daily** while still learning accounting codes.
His cash transfer comes after **paid household bills**, not out of the reserve.

steps.text: Check eleven light waste loads against signed weighbridge tickets Monday
Save 120 monthly only after wages pay mortgage, food and medicine

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Writing reports, checking weights, planning collections and answering managers are most of our week. A stronger system could do much of that and leave one clerk checking exceptions instead of four. The crew still moves food and flour, but my job is a report and a rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask for a paid trial on old waste tickets with the staff association representative present. I'd tell management to publish which posts and signatures stay before changing the team. I'd tell the night crew that a wrong number is their work being misdescribed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My junior lead layer may be folded into the finance office. I am curious enough to test the tool, but being a daily user does not make me a good accounts manager yet. Mira's kitchen wage and four months saved give us room to look, though my own wage still matters for the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In January I'd request a paid six-week trial on last quarter's tickets, only with director approval and the association representative's time funded. If it finds the empty-truck error and finance signs off, I'd put routine report drafts through it while a clerk checks source weights, but only after the director approves live use. I'd apply for posted reporting roles at the two nearby food firms after checking pay and hours, leaving this job only for a signed offer that keeps mortgage, food and medicine paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the team and my own post. The tool can catch a mistake and still leave fewer wages in the room.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the representative look for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Whether a worker can challenge a wrong load number before it appears in a performance report. The night crew should not carry blame for a form error. A faster report can spread a wrong number to more managers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you let the tool approve reports?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. Finance would check the test and the director would have to approve live use; a clerk would keep the original ticket beside the draft. I can automate the first version, not the signature. If those checks fail, we stay with the current process.

I'd demand a **published staffing plan** before desks change.
think: My **junior lead layer** could merge into finance.
Daily AI use does not make me **a strong accountant** yet.
do: Request a **paid six-week trial** only with director approval and funded association time.
Automate **routine report drafts** only after error test, finance sign-off, director rollout approval and human weight checks.
Apply for **posted local reporting roles** after pay and hours checks; leave only after affordable signed offer.
feel: I feel **anxious** about jobs despite a useful test.
S1.quote: A faster report can spread a wrong number to more managers.
fieldNote: His progressive view appears in **worker access** to challenge bad numbers.
Automation needs **finance and director approval** after a source-ticket test.
He can apply locally without treating another **reporting desk as safe**.

steps.text: Request paid waste-ticket trial only with director approval and funded association participation
Automate report drafts only after successful test, finance and director approval, retaining human weight checks
Apply for posted local reporting work with viable pay and hours; leave after signed offer

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2028 full AGI could read the tickets, write the report and plan collections better than our team. My own desk and the finance desk would face it then. The crew still carries spoiled flour until capable robots arrive around 2031, but I cannot claim I can step into their paid work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the clerks to ask for written notice and redeployment terms through the staff association. I'd tell Mira we should pause the planned new kitchen cabinets before a deposit. I'd tell managers they must keep a way to correct a false waste report.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my reporting post could end, but I don't know if the company would keep a human sign-off role. Mira's kitchen wage and our four months cash would pay essentials for a while if mine stopped, though we would have to cut extras. I would be worried about replacing my typical manager pay, but I can search without asking our children for rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'd ask the association representative to request written notice and redeployment terms and pause the cabinet deposit. If AGI arrives in 2028 and my post ends, I'd apply for posted local paid work only after checking the job's actual duties and pay; I'd take it only if the wage with Mira's confirmed hours covers mortgage, food and medicine. I'd keep my current pay until a signed offer if the job still exists, and check public support eligibility before applying if our combined income falls short.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, but not sleepless. Four months and Mira's wage let us make a careful list of real options.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you go back to deliveries?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could apply if a paid place opens, but collection planning and booking face AGI in 2028 too. Lifting flour is physical until robots around 2031, and I'd need the employer to judge whether my back and training fit the duty. A delivery van is not a pension plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your grown children help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our son and daughter have their own expenses. We can tell them why the cabinets are delayed, but I would not ask for regular mortgage money. If we needed a one-off loan, Mira and I would discuss it before asking whether either could afford one.

say: I'd ask for **written redeployment terms** through the association before any desks close.
I'd tell Mira the **cabinet deposit** must wait until we know my wage.
think: My **reporting post could end**, though a human sign-off role might remain.
Four months cash and Mira's pay give us **search time** if my wage stops.
do: Ask the **staff association** for notice terms; check public support eligibility if combined income falls short.
Pause the **kitchen-cabinet deposit** before paying it.
Apply for **posted local work** with actual duties and pay checked; accept only with affordable combined wages.
feel: I feel **anxious** about lost manager pay while able to plan.
S2.quote: A delivery van is not a pension plan.
fieldNote: He does not assume the **collection-planning desk** escapes 2028 AGI.
Four months cash and Mira's paid kitchen work protect **short-term essentials**.
Support applications depend on **verified eligibility** if combined income falls short.

steps.text: Ask association representative for written notice and redeployment terms
Pause kitchen-cabinet deposit before paying it
Apply for posted local work after duties and pay check; accept only with affordable combined wages
Check public support eligibility and apply only if household qualifies after income shortfall

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years could let us build more cash and check the pension before my reporting desk faces AGI in 2031. The night crew's physical lifting faces capable robots around 2034, while its rota and our reports change in 2031. I won't turn a three-year physical delay into a career promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the company and association to set real staffing dates. I'd tell Mira we should compare our pension statements with mortgage and food costs before talking about retirement. I'd tell the night crew their ticket records remain open to correction.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I may keep earning in reporting until 2031, but I still need to learn the accounting side. I don't know our pension eligibility or amounts, so I cannot say I can stop at sixty-three. Four months cash is useful, and I would prefer six before an uncertain wage change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2027 I'd request written pension eligibility dates and projected amounts for both of us and compare them with mortgage, food and medicine. I'd save 180 monthly only while both wages cover those bills, aiming for six months of expenses without promising a date. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2031, I'd apply for posted local paid work only if its wage with Mira's confirmed income covers essentials; I'd leave my present job only for a signed offer or verified pension income that truly covers the bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my pay after 2031, but the extra time helps. The pension number needs to be written down before I trust it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the estimate is small?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We keep working if paid roles exist, rather than call a small letter a pension. I would ask about public support only if we are eligible. I don't know what an age on a form will buy us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could the union get you a job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It can ask for fair notice and a real redeployment process, but it cannot create a vacancy. I would apply for an actual posted role and compare the wage. A union letter is not a signed job offer.

I'd tell Mira to check **both pension statements** against bills.
think: I may earn until 2031, but **pension eligibility** is unknown.
I would prefer **six months cash** before a wage change.
do: Request **both pension statements** in 2027 and compare with essentials.
Save **180 monthly** only while both wages pay mortgage, food and medicine.
Apply for **posted local work** after 2031 only with affordable combined income; leave after signed offer or adequate pension.
feel: I feel **anxious** about pay while the longer runway helps.
S3.quote: A union letter is not a signed job offer.
fieldNote: He distinguishes **worker representation** from a guaranteed vacancy.
The six-month cash target depends on **both wages** covering essentials.
He will not assume **pension eligibility** at sixty-three.

steps.text: Request written pension eligibility dates and amounts for both partners in 2027
Save 180 monthly only while both wages cover mortgage, food and medicine
Apply for local work with affordable combined income; leave after signed offer or verified sufficient pension

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: The next picture is called AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll be sixty-eight in 2036; our children will have their own lives and expenses. Our reports face AGI in 2036, and capable robots can lift and move spoiled food around 2039. I don't know whether either of us will have a pension large enough to stop work then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the company and association for annual staffing reviews with published dates. I'd tell Mira we should check the mortgage and pension figures every year. I'd tell the night crew that old weighbridge tickets must remain available for disputes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade gives us time to make the mortgage smaller and perhaps reach six months cash if both wages keep arriving. I might be able to retire at sixty-eight, but that depends on actual eligibility and amounts, not the calendar alone. My daily AI use does not make the reporting desk safe after 2036.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This winter I'd ask the pension provider for both eligibility dates and estimated monthly amounts, then compare the figures with mortgage, food and medicine. I'd pay 200 extra monthly against the mortgage only after retaining four months of cash and paying essentials from both wages, stopping if Mira's hours fall. In the first year after AGI arrives in 2036, I'd stop working only if actual pension income plus Mira's confirmed pay covers those bills; otherwise I'd apply for posted paid work with a wage and travel I can manage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the eventual desk change, but the decade offers time to put real numbers in a folder. I would not take a retirement photograph before checking the account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move near your children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They live in separate towns, and neither has offered us a home. We would move only if Mira agrees and a real job or pension plus an affordable home covers our costs. I would not make our children the housing plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the mortgage cannot be reduced?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then the 200 extra payment stops before it eats our four-month cash reserve. We would keep paying the ordinary mortgage if wages cover it and ask the lender about options before arrears. The pension and rent-equivalent housing costs still have to add up.

say: I'd ask for **annual staffing reviews** with published dates.
I'd tell Mira to compare **mortgage and pension** figures yearly.
think: I might retire at sixty-eight only if **pension eligibility and amounts** support it.
I can reduce debt only while **both wages continue**.
do: Request **pension dates and amounts** for both partners this winter.
Pay **200 extra monthly** on mortgage only while both wages cover essentials and four months cash remains; stop if Mira's hours fall.
Apply for **posted paid work** after 2036 if pension plus Mira's pay is insufficient and travel is manageable.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about the desk with time to plan.
S4.quote: I would not take a retirement photograph before checking the account.
fieldNote: He will not count a **birthday** as pension eligibility.
Mortgage overpayments stop if **Mira's hours** fall.
Later work still needs **actual pay** and manageable travel.

steps.text: Request written pension eligibility dates and monthly amounts for both partners
Pay 200 extra mortgage only while Mira's hours hold, essentials paid and four months cash remains
Apply for posted paid work if combined actual pension and Mira pay insufficient; require manageable travel

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it gives us little time to settle what happens to my reporting desk. Written notice and redeployment terms, real paid openings, and accurate pension statements would help. Mira's wage and our four months saved give us room to ask questions, not a reason to assume the job survives.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the night worker who loaded the spoiled flour what a false low-waste chart says about their shift. The signed ticket has grease on it, but it tells the truth. I want the worker able to challenge the chart before it goes to the board.

headlineQuote: The signed ticket has grease on it, but it tells the truth.
portrait: Tomas, **58**, is a junior lead of four food-waste reporting clerks after years in delivery coordination.
He uses AI **daily** but still learns accounting codes and checks original weighbridge tickets.
Typical pay, Mira's kitchen wage and **four months saved** support their mortgage; their grown children live separately.
He seeks **staff representation** and actual pension figures before any job or retirement decision.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** gives his reporting desk little time before possible change.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **written notice and redeployment** terms and actual paid openings.
He needs **accurate pension statements** for both partners before deciding when to stop work.
